transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you very much, Jim, and thanks to the commission and the University of Mississippi, Ole Miss, for hosting us tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I can’t think of a more important time for us to talk about the future of the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, we are at a defining moment in our history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Our nation is involved in two wars, and we are going through the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And although we’ve heard a lot about Wall Street, those of you on Main Street I think have been struggling for a while, and you recognize that this could have an impact on all sectors of the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you’re wondering, how’s it going to affect me?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: How’s it going to affect my job?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: How’s it going to affect my house?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: How’s it going to affect my retirement savings or my ability to send my children to college?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we have to move swiftly, and we have to move wisely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve put forward a series of proposals that make sure that we protect taxpayers as we engage in this important rescue effort.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, we’ve got to make sure that we’ve got oversight over this whole process; $700 billion, potentially, is a lot of money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we’ve got to make sure that taxpayers, when they are putting their money at risk, have the possibility of getting that money back and gains, if the market — and when the market returns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number three, we’ve got to make sure that none of that money is going to pad CEO bank accounts or to promote golden parachutes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, number four, we’ve got to make sure that we’re helping homeowners, because the root problem here has to do with the foreclosures that are taking place all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, we also have to recognize that this is a final verdict on eight years of failed economic policies promoted by George Bush, supported by Senator McCain, a theory that basically says that we can shred regulations and consumer protections and give more and more to the most, and somehow prosperity will trickle down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It hasn’t worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that the fundamentals of the economy have to be measured by whether or not the middle class is getting a fair shake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’m running for president, and that’s what I hope we’re going to be talking about tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And thanks to everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I do have a sad note tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Kennedy is in the hospital.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He’s a dear and beloved friend to all of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Our thoughts and prayers go out to the lion of the Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I also want to thank the University of Mississippi for hosting us tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, Jim, I — I’ve been not feeling too great about a lot of things lately.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So have a lot of Americans who are facing challenges.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I’m feeling a little better tonight, and I’ll tell you why.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because as we’re here tonight in this debate, we are seeing, for the first time in a long time, Republicans and Democrats together, sitting down, trying to work out a solution to this fiscal crisis that we’re in.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And have no doubt about the magnitude of this crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’re not talking about failure of institutions on Wall Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re talking about failures on Main Street, and people who will lose their jobs, and their credits, and their homes, if we don’t fix the greatest fiscal crisis, probably in — certainly in our time, and I’ve been around a little while.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the point is — the point is, we have finally seen Republicans and Democrats sitting down and negotiating together and coming up with a package.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This package has transparency in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It has to have accountability and oversight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It has to have options for loans to failing businesses, rather than the government taking over those loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to — it has to have a package with a number of other essential elements to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, yes, I went back to Washington, and I met with my Republicans in the House of Representatives.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they weren’t part of the negotiations, and I understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it was the House Republicans that decided that they would be part of the solution to this problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I want to emphasize one point to all Americans tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This isn’t the beginning of the end of this crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This is the end of the beginning, if we come out with a package that will keep these institutions stable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a lot of work to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And one of the areas, of course, is to eliminate our dependence on foreign oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t seen the language yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I do think that there’s constructive work being done out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, for the viewers who are watching, I am optimistic about the capacity of us to come together with a plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The question, I think, that we have to ask ourselves is, how did we get into this situation in the first place?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Two years ago, I warned that, because of the subprime lending mess, because of the lax regulation, that we were potentially going to have a problem and tried to stop some of the abuses in mortgages that were taking place at the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Last year, I wrote to the secretary of the Treasury to make sure that he understood the magnitude of this problem and to call on him to bring all the stakeholders together to try to deal with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So — so the question, I think, that we’ve got to ask ourselves is, yes, we’ve got to solve this problem short term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are going to have to intervene; there’s no doubt about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’re also going to have to look at, how is it that we shredded so many regulations?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We did not set up a 21st-century regulatory framework to deal with these problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that in part has to do with an economic philosophy that says that regulation is always bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I — I hope so.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But — but let me — let me point out, I also warned about Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and warned about corporate greed and excess, and CEO pay, and all that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: A lot of us saw this train wreck coming.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But there’s also the issue of responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’ve mentioned President Dwight David Eisenhower.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: President Eisenhower, on the night before the Normandy invasion, went into his room, and he wrote out two letters.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: One of them was a letter congratulating the great members of the military and allies that had conducted and succeeded in the greatest invasion in history, still to this day, and forever.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And he wrote out another letter, and that was a letter of resignation from the United States Army for the failure of the landings at Normandy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Somehow we’ve lost that accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been heavily criticized because I called for the resignation of the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to start also holding people accountable, and we’ve got to reward people who succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But somehow in Washington today — and I’m afraid on Wall Street — greed is rewarded, excess is rewarded, and corruption — or certainly failure to carry out our responsibility is rewarded.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As president of the United States, people are going to be held accountable in my administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I promise you that that will happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think Senator McCain’s absolutely right that we need more responsibility, but we need it not just when there’s a crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we’ve had years in which the reigning economic ideology has been what’s good for Wall Street, but not what’s good for Main Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And there are folks out there who’ve been struggling before this crisis took place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why it’s so important, as we solve this short-term problem, that we look at some of the underlying issues that have led to wages and incomes for ordinary Americans to go down, the — a health care system that is broken, energy policies that are not working, because, you know, 10 days ago, John said that the fundamentals of the economy are sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do not think that they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, the — John, 10 days ago, you said that the fundamentals of the economy are sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Are you afraid I couldn’t hear him?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The — and I just fundamentally disagree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And unless we are holding ourselves accountable day in, day out, not just when there’s a crisis for folks who have power and influence and can hire lobbyists, but for the nurse, the teacher, the police officer, who, frankly, at the end of each month, they’ve got a little financial crisis going on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’re having to take out extra debt just to make their mortgage payments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t been paying attention to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if you look at our tax policies, it’s a classic example.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: No, I — look, we’ve got to fix the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got fundamental problems in the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Main Street is paying a penalty for the excesses and greed in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: , and in the Wall Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So there’s no doubt that we have a long way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, obviously, stricter interpretation and consolidation of the various regulatory agencies that weren’t doing their job, that has brought on this crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I have a fundamental belief in the goodness and strength of the American worker.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the American worker is the most productive, the most innovative.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: America is still the greatest producer, exporter and importer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve got to get through these times, but I have a fundamental belief in the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I still believe, under the right leadership, our best days are ahead of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, the first thing we have to do is get spending under control in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s completely out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s gone — we have now presided over the largest increase in the size of government since the Great Society.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We Republicans came to power to change government, and government changed us.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the — the worst symptom on this disease is what my friend, Tom Coburn, calls earmarking as a gateway drug, because it’s a gateway.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s a gateway to out-of-control spending and corruption.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we have former members of Congress now residing in federal prison because of the evils of this earmarking and pork-barrel spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, we spent $3 million to study the DNA of bears in Montana.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know if that was a criminal issue or a paternal issue, but the fact is that it was $3 million of our taxpayers’ money.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it has got to be brought under control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As president of the United States, I want to assure you, I’ve got a pen.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This one’s kind of old.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a pen, and I’m going to veto every single spending bill that comes across my desk.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I will make them famous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You will know their names.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator Obama, you wanted to know one of the differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He has asked for $932 million of earmark pork-barrel spending, nearly a million dollars for every day that he’s been in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I suggest that people go up on the Web site of Citizens Against Government Waste, and they’ll look at those projects.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That kind of thing is not the way to rein in runaway spending in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s one of the fundamental differences that Senator Obama and I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Senator McCain is absolutely right that the earmarks process has been abused, which is why I suspended any requests for my home state, whether it was for senior centers or what have you, until we cleaned it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And he’s also right that oftentimes lobbyists and special interests are the ones that are introducing these kinds of requests, although that wasn’t the case with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But let’s be clear: Earmarks account for $18 billion in last year’s budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain is proposing — and this is a fundamental difference between us — $300 billion in tax cuts to some of the wealthiest corporations and individuals in the country, $300 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, $18 billion is important; $300 billion is really important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in his tax plan, you would have CEOs of Fortune 500 companies getting an average of $700,000 in reduced taxes, while leaving 100 million Americans out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So my attitude is, we’ve got to grow the economy from the bottom up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve called for is a tax cut for 95 percent of working families, 95 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means that the ordinary American out there who’s collecting a paycheck every day, they’ve got a little extra money to be able to buy a computer for their kid, to fill up on this gas that is killing them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And over time, that, I think, is going to be a better recipe for economic growth than the — the policies of President Bush that John McCain wants to — wants to follow.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, again, I don’t mean to go back and forth, but he…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama suspended those requests for pork-barrel projects after he was running for president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t happen to see that light during the first three years as a member of the United States Senate, $932 million in requests.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Maybe to Senator Obama it’s not a lot of money.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the point is that — you see, I hear this all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: “It’s only $18 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” Do you know that it’s tripled in the last five years?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Do you know that it’s gone completely out of control to the point where it corrupts people?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It corrupts people.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we have, as I said, people under federal indictment and charges.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s a system that’s got to be cleaned up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought against it my career.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I was called the sheriff, by the — one of the senior members of the Appropriations Committee.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t win Miss Congeniality in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator Obama didn’t mention that, along with his tax cuts, he is also proposing some $800 billion in new spending on new programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s a fundamental difference between myself and Senator Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to cut spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to keep taxes low.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The worst thing we could do in this economic climate is to raise people’s taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I — I don’t know where John is getting his figures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s just be clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I do is I close corporate loopholes, stop providing tax cuts to corporations that are shipping jobs overseas so that we’re giving tax breaks to companies that are investing here in the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I make sure that we have a health care system that allows for everyone to have basic coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think those are pretty important priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I pay for every dime of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But let’s go back to the original point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: John, nobody is denying that $18 billion is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, absolutely, we need earmark reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when I’m president, I will go line by line to make sure that we are not spending money unwisely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But the fact is that eliminating earmarks alone is not a recipe for how we’re going to get the middle class back on track.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when you look at your tax policies that are directed primarily at those who are doing well, and you are neglecting people who are really struggling right now, I think that is a continuation of the last eight years, and we can’t afford another four.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well — well, let me give you an example of what Senator Obama finds objectionable, the business tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Right now, in the United States of America, business pays the second-highest business taxes in the world, 35 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Ireland pays 11 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you’re a business person, and you can locate any place in the world, then, obviously, if you go to the country where it’s 11 percent tax versus 35 percent, you’re going to be able to create jobs, increase your business, make more investment, et cetera.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to cut that business tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to cut it so that businesses will remain in — in the United States of America and create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But, again, I want to return.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s a lot more than $18 billion in pork-barrel spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I can tell you, it’s rife.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s throughout.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The United States Senate will take up a continuing resolution tomorrow or the next day, sometime next week, with 2,000 — 2,000 — look at them, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look at them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’ll be appalled.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Senator Obama is a recent convert, after requesting $932 million worth of pork-barrel spending projects.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So the point is, I want people to have tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want every family to have a $5,000 refundable tax credit so they can go out and purchase their own health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to double the dividend from $3,500 to $7,000 for every dependent child in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know that the worst thing we could possibly do is to raise taxes on anybody, and a lot of people might be interested in Senator Obama’s definition of “rich.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just make a couple of points.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My definition — here’s what I can tell the American people: 95 percent of you will get a tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if you make less than $250,000, less than a quarter-million dollars a year, then you will not see one dime’s worth of tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, John mentioned the fact that business taxes on paper are high in this country, and he’s absolutely right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Here’s the problem: There are so many loopholes that have been written into the tax code, oftentimes with support of Senator McCain, that we actually see our businesses pay effectively one of the lowest tax rates in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what that means, then, is that there are people out there who are working every day, who are not getting a tax cut, and you want to give them more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not like you want to close the loopholes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You just want to add an additional tax cut over the loopholes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s a problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Just one last point I want to make, since Senator McCain talked about providing a $5,000 health credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, what he doesn’t tell you is that he intends to, for the first time in history, tax health benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So you may end up getting a $5,000 tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Here’s the only problem: Your employer now has to pay taxes on the health care that you’re getting from your employer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if you end up losing your health care from your employer, you’ve got to go out on the open market and try to buy it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is not a good deal for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it’s an example of this notion that the market can always solve everything and that the less regulation we have, the better off we’re going to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, let me just…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know we have to, but this is a classic example of walking the walk and talking the talk.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We had an energy bill before the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It was festooned with Christmas tree ornaments.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It had all kinds of breaks for the oil companies, I mean, billions of dollars worth.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I voted against it; Senator Obama voted for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: John, you want to give oil companies another $4 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to look at our record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to look at our records.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s the important thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Who fought against wasteful and earmark spending?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Who has been the person who has tried to keep spending under control?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Who’s the person who has believed that the best thing for America is — is to have a tax system that is fundamentally fair?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve fought to simplify it, and I have proposals to simplify it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s give every American a choice: two tax brackets, generous dividends, and, two — and let Americans choose whether they want the — the existing tax code or they want a new tax code.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And so, again, look at the record, particularly the energy bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But, again, Senator Obama has shifted on a number of occasions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He has voted in the United States Senate to increase taxes on people who make as low as $42,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true, John.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s just a fact.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Again, you can look it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, it’s just not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we want to talk about oil company profits, under your tax plan, John — this is undeniable — oil companies would get an additional $4 billion in tax breaks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, look, we all would love to lower taxes on everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But here’s the problem: If we are giving them to oil companies, then that means that there are those who are not going to be getting them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: With all due respect, you already gave them to the oil companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, but, John, the fact of the matter is, is that I was opposed to those tax breaks, tried to strip them out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got an energy bill on the Senate floor right now that contains some good stuff, some stuff you want, including drilling off-shore, but you’re opposed to it because it would strip away those tax breaks that have gone to oil companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, there are a range of things that are probably going to have to be delayed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We don’t yet know what our tax revenues are going to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The economy is slowing down, so it’s hard to anticipate right now what the budget is going to look like next year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there’s no doubt that we’re not going to be able to do everything that I think needs to be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There are some things that I think have to be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have to have energy independence, so I’ve put forward a plan to make sure that, in 10 years’ time, we have freed ourselves from dependence on Middle Eastern oil by increasing production at home, but most importantly by starting to invest in alternative energy, solar, wind, biodiesel, making sure that we’re developing the fuel-efficient cars of the future right here in the United States, in Ohio and Michigan, instead of Japan and South Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have to fix our health care system, which is putting an enormous burden on families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Just — a report just came out that the average deductible went up 30 percent on American families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are getting crushed, and many of them are going bankrupt as a consequence of health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m meeting folks all over the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have to do that now, because it will actually make our businesses and our families better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The third thing we have to do is we’ve got to make sure that we’re competing in education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to invest in science and technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: China had a space launch and a space walk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to make sure that our children are keeping pace in math and in science.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things I think we have to do is make sure that college is affordable for every young person in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I also think that we’re going to have to rebuild our infrastructure, which is falling behind, our roads, our bridges, but also broadband lines that reach into rural communities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Also, making sure that we have a new electricity grid to get the alternative energy to population centers that are using them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So there are some — some things that we’ve got to do structurally to make sure that we can compete in this global economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t shortchange those things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to eliminate programs that don’t work, and we’ve got to make sure that the programs that we do have are more efficient and cost less.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, we, no matter what, we’ve got to cut spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have — as I said, we’ve let government get completely out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has the most liberal voting record in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s hard to reach across the aisle from that far to the left.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The point — the point is — the point is, we need to examine every agency of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: First of all, by the way, I’d eliminate ethanol subsidies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I oppose ethanol subsidies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think that we have to return — particularly in defense spending, which is the largest part of our appropriations — we have to do away with cost-plus contracts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We now have defense systems that the costs are completely out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We tried to build a little ship called the Littoral Combat Ship that was supposed to cost $140 million, ended up costing $400 million, and we still haven’t done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So we need to have fixed-cost contracts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need very badly to understand that defense spending is very important and vital, particularly in the new challenges we face in the world, but we have to get a lot of the cost overruns under control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I saved the taxpayers $6.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: 8 billion by fighting a contract that was negotiated between Boeing and DOD that was completely wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we fixed it and we killed it and the people ended up in federal prison so I know how to do this because I’ve been involved these issues for many, many years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I think that we have to examine every agency of government and find out those that are doing their job and keep them and find out those that aren’t and eliminate them and we’ll have to scrub every agency of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: As I said before, Jim, there are going to be things that end up having to be …

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … deferred and delayed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, look, I want to make sure that we are investing in energy in order to free ourselves from the dependence on foreign oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is a big project.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is a multi-year project.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not willing to give up the need to do it but there may be individual components that we can’t do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But John is right we have to make cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We right now give $15 billion every year as subsidies to private insurers under the Medicare system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Doesn’t work any better through the private insurers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They just skim off $15 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That was a give away and part of the reason is because lobbyists are able to shape how Medicare works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They did it on the Medicaid prescription drug bill and we have to change the culture.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Tom — or John mentioned me being wildly liberal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Mostly that’s just me opposing George Bush’s wrong headed policies since I’ve been in Congress but I think it is that it is also important to recognize I worked with Tom Coburn, the most conservative, one of the most conservative Republicans who John already mentioned to set up what we call a Google for government saying we’ll list every dollar of federal spending to make sure that the taxpayer can take a look and see who, in fact, is promoting some of these spending projects that John’s been railing about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: How about a spending freeze on everything but defense, veteran affairs and entitlement programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to seriously consider with the exceptions of caring for our veterans national defense and several other vital issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The problem with a spending freeze is you’re using a hatchet where you need a scalpel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There are some programs that are very important that are under funded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I went to increase early childhood education and the notion that we should freeze that when there may be, for example, this Medicare subsidy, I think, doesn’t make sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you another place to look for some savings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are currently spending $10 billion a month in Iraq when they have a $79 billion surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It seems to me that if we’re going to be strong at home as well as strong abroad, that we have to look at bringing that war to a close.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, we are sending $700 billion a year overseas to countries that don’t like us very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Some of that money ends up in the hands of terrorist organizations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to have wind, tide, solar, natural gas, flex fuel cars and all that but we also have to have offshore drilling and we also have to have nuclear power.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama opposes both storing and reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You can’t get there from here and the fact is that we can create 700,000 jobs by building constructing 45 new nuclear power plants by the year 2030.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Nuclear power is not only important as far as eliminating our dependence on foreign oil but it’s also responsibility as far as climate change is concerned.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: An issue I have been involved in for many, many years and I’m proud of the work of the work that I’ve done there along with Senator Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt itâ€™s gonna affect our budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There is no doubt about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not only — Even if we get all $700 billion back, let’s assume the markets recover, we’re holding assets long enough that eventually taxpayers get it back and that happened during the Great Depression when Roosevelt purchased a whole bunch of homes, over time, home values went back up and in fact government made a profit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we’re lucky and we do it right, that could potentially happen but in the short term there’s an outlay and we may not see that money for a while.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And because of the economy’s slowing down, I think we can also expect less tax revenue so there’s no doubt that as president I’m going to have to make some tough decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The only point I want to make is this, that in order to make those tough decisions we have to know what our values are and who we’re fighting for and what our priorities are and if we are spending $300 billion on tax cuts for people who don’t need them and weren’t even asking for them, and we are leaving out health care which is crushing on people all across the country, then I think we have made a bad decision and I want to make sure we’re not shortchanging our long term priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, I want to make sure we’re not handing the health care system over to the federal government which is basically what would ultimately happen with Senator Obama’s health care plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want the families to make decisions between themselves and their doctors.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Not the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to obviously cut spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought to cut spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has $800 billion in new spending programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would suggest he start by canceling some of those new spending program that he has.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can’t I think adjust spending around to take care of the very much needed programs, including taking care of our veterans but I also want to say again a healthy economy with low taxes would not raising anyone’s taxes is probably the best recipe for eventually having our economy recover.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And spending restraint has got to be a vital part of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the reason, one of the major reasons why we’re in the difficulties we are in today is because spending got out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We owe China $500 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And spending, I know, can be brought under control because I have fought against excessive spending my entire career.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I got plans to reduce and eliminate unnecessary and wasteful spending and if there’s anybody here who thinks there aren’t agencies of government where spending can be cut and their budgets slashed they have not spent a lot of time in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I just want to make this point, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: John, it’s been your president who you said you agreed with 90 percent of the time who presided over this increase in spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This orgy of spending and enormous deficits you voted for almost all of his budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So to stand here and after eight years and say that you’re going to lead on controlling spending and, you know, balancing our tax cuts so that they help middle class families when over the last eight years that hasn’t happened I think just is, you know, kind of hard to swallow.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s well-known that I have not been elected Miss Congeniality in the United States Senate nor with the administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have opposed the president on spending, on climate change, on torture of prisoner, on – on Guantanamo Bay.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: On a — on the way that the Iraq War was conducted.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a long record and the American people know me very well and that is independent and a maverick of the Senate and I’m happy to say that I’ve got a partner that’s a good maverick along with me now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think the lessons of Iraq are very clear that you cannot have a failed strategy that will then cause you to nearly lose a conflict.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Our initial military success, we went in to Baghdad and everybody celebrated.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And then the war was very badly mishandled.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I went to Iraq in 2003 and came back and said, we’ve got to change this strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This strategy requires additional troops, it requires a fundamental change in strategy and I fought for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And finally, we came up with a great general and a strategy that has succeeded.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This strategy has succeeded.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we are winning in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we will come home with victory and with honor.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that withdrawal is the result of every counterinsurgency that succeeds.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I want to tell you that now that we will succeed and our troops will come home, and not in defeat, that we will see a stable ally in the region and a fledgling democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The consequences of defeat would have been increased Iranian influence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It would have been increase in sectarian violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It would have been a wider war, which the United States of America might have had to come back.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So there was a lot at stake there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And thanks to this great general, David Petraeus, and the troops who serve under him, they have succeeded.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we are winning in Iraq, and we will come home.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we will come home as we have when we have won other wars and not in defeat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, this is an area where Senator McCain and I have a fundamental difference because I think the first question is whether we should have gone into the war in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now six years ago, I stood up and opposed this war at a time when it was politically risky to do so because I said that not only did we not know how much it was going to cost, what our exit strategy might be, how it would affect our relationships around the world, and whether our intelligence was sound, but also because we hadn’t finished the job in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We hadn’t caught bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We hadn’t put al Qaeda to rest, and as a consequence, I thought that it was going to be a distraction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now Senator McCain and President Bush had a very different judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I wish I had been wrong for the sake of the country and they had been right, but that’s not the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve spent over $600 billion so far, soon to be $1 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have lost over 4,000 lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have seen 30,000 wounded, and most importantly, from a strategic national security perspective, al Qaeda is resurgent, stronger now than at any time since 2001.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We took our eye off the ball.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And not to mention that we are still spending $10 billion a month, when they have a $79 billion surplus, at a time when we are in great distress here at home, and we just talked about the fact that our budget is way overstretched and we are borrowing money from overseas to try to finance just some of the basic functions of our government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So I think the lesson to be drawn is that we should never hesitate to use military force, and I will not, as president, in order to keep the American people safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we have to use our military wisely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we did not use our military wisely in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The next president of the United States is not going to have to address the issue as to whether we went into Iraq or not.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The next president of the United States is going to have to decide how we leave, when we leave, and what we leave behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s the decision of the next president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama said the surge could not work, said it would increase sectarian violence, said it was doomed to failure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Recently on a television program, he said it exceed our wildest expectations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But yet, after conceding that, he still says that he would oppose the surge if he had to decide that again today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Incredibly, incredibly Senator Obama didn’t go to Iraq for 900 days and never asked for a meeting with General Petraeus.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama is the chairperson of a committee that oversights NATO that’s in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: To this day, he has never had a hearing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I mean, it’s remarkable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Which point?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He raised a whole bunch of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, I’m very proud of my vice presidential selection, Joe Biden, who is the chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and as he explains, and as John well knows, the issues of Afghanistan, the issues of Iraq, critical issues like that, don’t go through my subcommittee because they’re done as a committee as a whole.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But that’s Senate inside baseball.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But let’s get back to the core issue here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain is absolutely right that the violence has been reduced as a consequence of the extraordinary sacrifice of our troops and our military families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They have done a brilliant job, and General Petraeus has done a brilliant job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But understand, that was a tactic designed to contain the damage of the previous four years of mismanagement of this war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so John likes — John, you like to pretend like the war started in 2007.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You talk about the surge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The war started in 2003, and at the time when the war started, you said it was going to be quick and easy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You said we knew where the weapons of mass destruction were.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You were wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You said that we were going to be greeted as liberators.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You were wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You said that there was no history of violence between Shia and Sunni.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you were wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so my question is…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … of judgment, of whether or not — of whether or not — if the question is who is best-equipped as the next president to make good decisions about how we use our military, how we make sure that we are prepared and ready for the next conflict, then I think we can take a look at our judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m afraid Senator Obama doesn’t understand the difference between a tactic and a strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the important — I’d like to tell you, two Fourths of July ago I was in Baghdad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: General Petraeus invited Senator Lindsey Graham and me to attend a ceremony where 688 brave young Americans, whose enlistment had expired, were reenlisting to stay and fight for Iraqi freedom and American freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I was honored to be there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I was honored to speak to those troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And you know, afterwards, we spent a lot of time with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And you know what they said to us?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They said, let us win.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They said, let us win.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We don’t want our kids coming back here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And this strategy, and this general, they are winning.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama refuses to acknowledge that we are winning in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They just passed an electoral…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: An election law just in the last few days.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There is social, economic progress, and a strategy, a strategy of going into an area, clearing and holding, and the people of the country then become allied with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They inform on the bad guys.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And peace comes to the country, and prosperity.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what’s happening in Iraq, and it wasn’t a tactic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Jim, Jim, this is a big…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It was a strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that same strategy will be employed in Afghanistan by this great general.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Senator Obama, who after promising not to vote to cut off funds for the troops, did the incredible thing of voting to cut off the funds for the troops in Iraq and Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Jim, there are a whole bunch of things we have got to answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, let’s talk about this troop funding issue because John always brings this up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain cut — Senator McCain opposed funding for troops in legislation that had a timetable, because he didn’t believe in a timetable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I opposed funding a mission that had no timetable, and was open- ended, giving a blank check to George Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We had a difference on the timetable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t have a difference on whether or not we were going to be funding troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We had a legitimate difference, and I absolutely understand the difference between tactics and strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the strategic question that the president has to ask is not whether or not we are employing a particular approach in the country once we have made the decision to be there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The question is, was this wise?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have seen Afghanistan worsen, deteriorate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need more troops there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need more resources there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain, in the rush to go into Iraq, said, you know what?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been successful in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There is nobody who can pose a threat to us there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is a time when bin Laden was still out, and now they’ve reconstituted themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Secretary of Defense Robert Gates himself acknowledges the war on terrorism started in Afghanistan and it needs to end there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we can’t do it if we are not willing to give Iraq back its country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, what I’ve said is we should end this war responsibly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We should do it in phases.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But in 16 months we should be able to reduce our combat troops, put — provide some relief to military families and our troops and bolster our efforts in Afghanistan so that we can capture and kill bin Laden and crush al Qaeda.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And right now, the commanders in Afghanistan, as well as Admiral Mullen, have acknowledged that we don’t have enough troops to deal with Afghanistan because we still have more troops in Iraq than we did before the surge.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Admiral Mullen suggests that Senator Obama’s plan is dangerous for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what …

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What he said was a precipitous…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what Admiral Mullen said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … withdrawal would be dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He did not say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And also General Petraeus said the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Osama bin Laden and General Petraeus have one thing in common that I know of, they both said that Iraq is the central battleground.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now General Petraeus has praised the successes, but he said those successes are fragile and if we set a specific date for withdrawal — and by the way, Senator Obama’s original plan, they would have been out last spring before the surge ever had a chance to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’m — I’m — understand why Senator Obama was surprised and said that the surge succeeded beyond his wildest expectations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It didn’t exceed beyond mine, because I know that that’s a strategy that has worked and can succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But if we snatch defeat from the jaws of victory and adopt Senator Obama’s plan, then we will have a wider war and it will make things more complicated throughout the region, including in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I think we need more troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been saying that for over a year now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that we have to do it as quickly as possible, because it’s been acknowledged by the commanders on the ground the situation is getting worse, not better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We had the highest fatalities among U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: troops this past year than at any time since 2002.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are seeing a major offensive taking place — Al Qaida and Taliban crossing the border and attacking our troops in a brazen fashion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are feeling emboldened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we cannot separate Afghanistan from Iraq, because what our commanders have said is we don’t have the troops right now to deal with Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So I would send two to three additional brigades to Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, keep in mind that we have four times the number of troops in Iraq, where nobody had anything to do with 9/11 before we went in, where, in fact, there was no Al Qaida before we went in, but we have four times more troops there than we do in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that is a strategic mistake, because every intelligence agency will acknowledge that Al Qaida is the greatest threat against the United States and that Secretary of Defense Gates acknowledged the central front — that the place where we have to deal with these folks is going to be in Afghanistan and in Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So here’s what we have to do comprehensively, though.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not just more troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have to press the Afghan government to make certain that they are actually working for their people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve said this to President Karzai.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we’ve got to deal with a growing poppy trade that has exploded over the last several years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number three, we’ve got to deal with Pakistan, because Al Qaida and the Taliban have safe havens in Pakistan, across the border in the northwest regions, and although, you know, under George Bush, with the support of Senator McCain, we’ve been giving them $10 billion over the last seven years, they have not done what needs to be done to get rid of those safe havens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And until we do, Americans here at home are not going to be safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I won’t repeat the mistake that I regret enormously, and that is, after we were able to help the Afghan freedom fighters and drive the Russians out of Afghanistan, we basically washed our hands of the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the result over time was the Taliban, Al Qaida, and a lot of the difficulties we are facing today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So we can’t ignore those lessons of history.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, on this issue of aiding Pakistan, if you’re going to aim a gun at somebody, George Shultz, our great secretary of state, told me once, you’d better be prepared to pull the trigger.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m not prepared at this time to cut off aid to Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I’m not prepared to threaten it, as Senator Obama apparently wants to do, as he has said that he would announce military strikes into Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to get the support of the people of — of Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He said that he would launch military strikes into Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, you don’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You don’t say that out loud.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If you have to do things, you have to do things, and you work with the Pakistani government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, the new president of Pakistan, Kardari , has got his hands full.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And this area on the border has not been governed since the days of Alexander the Great.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been to Waziristan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I can see how tough that terrain is.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s ruled by a handful of tribes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, yes, Senator Obama calls for more troops, but what he doesn’t understand, it’s got to be a new strategy, the same strategy that he condemned in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to have to be employed in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to have to help the Pakistanis go into these areas and obtain the allegiance of the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s going to be tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’ve intermarried with Al Qaida and the Taliban.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s going to be tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we have to get the cooperation of the people in those areas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the Pakistanis are going to have to understand that that bombing in the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad was a signal from the terrorists that they don’t want that government to cooperate with us in combating the Taliban and jihadist elements.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got a lot of work to do in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I’m confident, now that General Petraeus is in the new position of command, that we will employ a strategy which not only means additional troops — and, by the way, there have been 20,000 additional troops, from 32,000 to 53,000, and there needs to be more.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So it’s not just the addition of troops that matters.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s a strategy that will succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Pakistan is a very important element in this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I know how to work with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I guarantee you I would not publicly state that I’m going to attack them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nobody talked about attacking Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Here’s what I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if John wants to disagree with this, he can let me know, that, if the United States has Al Qaida, bin Laden, top-level lieutenants in our sights, and Pakistan is unable or unwilling to act, then we should take them out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think that’s the right strategy; I think that’s the right policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, John, I — you’re absolutely right that presidents have to be prudent in what they say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, you know, coming from you, who, you know, in the past has threatened extinction for North Korea and, you know, sung songs about bombing Iran, I don’t know, you know, how credible that is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think this is the right strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain is also right that it’s difficult.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is not an easy situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got cross-border attacks against U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We could allow our troops to just be on the defensive and absorb those blows again and again and again, if Pakistan is unwilling to cooperate, or we have to start making some decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the problem, John, with the strategy that’s been pursued was that, for 10 years, we coddled Musharraf, we alienated the Pakistani population, because we were anti-democratic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We had a 20th-century mindset that basically said, “Well, you know, he may be a dictator, but he’s our dictator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And as a consequence, we lost legitimacy in Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We spent $10 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in the meantime, they weren’t going after Al Qaida, and they are more powerful now than at any time since we began the war in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to change when I’m president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I — I don’t think that Senator Obama understands that there was a failed state in Pakistan when Musharraf came to power.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Everybody who was around then, and had been there, and knew about it knew that it was a failed state.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But let me tell you, you know, this business about bombing Iran and all that, let me tell you my record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Back in 1983, when I was a brand-new United States congressman, the one — the person I admired the most and still admire the most, Ronald Reagan, wanted to send Marines into Lebanon.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I saw that, and I saw the situation, and I stood up, and I voted against that, because I was afraid that they couldn’t make peace in a place where 300 or 400 or several hundred Marines would make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Tragically, I was right: Nearly 300 Marines lost their lives in the bombing of the barracks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And then we had Somalia — then we had the first Gulf War.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I supported — I supported that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I supported us going into Bosnia, when a number of my own party and colleagues was against that operation in Bosnia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
