transcript_turns.text: That was the right thing to do, to stop genocide and to preserve what was necessary inside of Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I supported what we did in Kosovo.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I supported it because ethnic cleansing and genocide was taking place there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I have a record — and Somalia, I opposed that we should turn — turn the force in Somalia from a peacekeeping force into a peacemaking force, which they were not capable of.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I have a record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a record of being involved in these national security issues, which involve the highest responsibility and the toughest decisions that any president can make, and that is to send our young men and women into harm’s way.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you, I had a town hall meeting in Wolfeboro, New Hampshire, and a woman stood up and she said, “Senator McCain, I want you to do me the honor of wearing a bracelet with my son’s name on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” He was 22 years old and he was killed in combat outside of Baghdad, Matthew Stanley, before Christmas last year.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This was last August, a year ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I said, “I will — I will wear his bracelet with honor.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” And this was August, a year ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And then she said, “But, Senator McCain, I want you to do everything — promise me one thing, that you’ll do everything in your power to make sure that my son’s death was not in vain.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” That means that that mission succeeds, just like those young people who re-enlisted in Baghdad, just like the mother I met at the airport the other day whose son was killed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they all say to me that we don’t want defeat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know what thatâ€™s like when an army is defeated.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: A war that I was in, where we had an Army, that it wasn’t through any fault of their own, but they were defeated.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I know how hard it is for that — for an Army and a military to recover from that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it did and we will win this one and we won’t come home in defeat and dishonor and probably have to go back if we fail.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Jim, let me just make a point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a bracelet, too, from Sergeant – from the mother of Sergeant Ryan David Jopeck , given to me in green bay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: She asked me, can you please make sure another mother is not going through what I’m going through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: soldier ever dies in vain because they’re carrying out the missions of their commander in chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we honor all the service that they’ve provided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Our troops have performed brilliantly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The question is for the next president, are we making good judgments about how to keep America safe precisely because sending our military into battle is such an enormous step.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the point that I originally made is that we took our eye off Afghanistan, we took our eye off the folks who perpetrated 9/11, they are still sending out videotapes and Senator McCain, nobody is talking about defeat in Iraq, but I have to say we are having enormous problems in Afghanistan because of that decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it is not true you have consistently been concerned about what happened in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: At one point, while you were focused on Iraq, you said well, we can “muddle through” Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You don’t muddle through the central front on terror and you don’t muddle through going after bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You don’t muddle through stamping out the Taliban.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that is something we have to take seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when I’m president, I will.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You might think that with that kind of concern that Senator Obama would have gone to Afghanistan, particularly given his responsibilities as a subcommittee chairman.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: By the way, when I’m subcommittee chairman, we take up the issues under my subcommittee.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the important thing is — the important thing is I visited Afghanistan and I traveled to Waziristan and I traveled to these places and I know what our security requirements are.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know what our needs are.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So the point is that we will prevail in Afghanistan, but we need the new strategy and we need it to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the important thing is, if we suffer defeat in Iraq, which General Petraeus predicts we will, if we adopted Senator Obama’s set date for withdrawal, then that will have a calamitous effect in Afghanistan and American national security interests in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama doesn’t seem to understand there is a connected between the two.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: A testimony to you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My reading of the threat from Iran is that if Iran acquires nuclear weapons, it is an existential threat to the State of Israel and it is a threat to other countries in the region because the other countries in the region will feel compelling requirement to acquire nuclear weapons as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now we cannot allow a second Holocaust.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s just make that very clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: What I have proposed for a long time, and I’ve had conversation with foreign leaders about forming a league of democracies, let’s be clear and let’s have some straight talk.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The Russians are preventing significant action in the United Nations Security Council.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have proposed a league of democracies, a group of people – a group of countries that share common interests, common values, common ideals, they also control a lot of the world’s economic power.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We could impose significant meaningful, painful sanctions on the Iranians that I think could have a beneficial effect.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The Iranians have a lousy government, so therefore their economy is lousy, even though they have significant oil revenues.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I am convinced that together, we can, with the French, with the British, with the Germans and other countries, democracies around the world, we can affect Iranian behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But have no doubt, but have no doubt that the Iranians continue on the path to the acquisition of a nuclear weapon as we speak tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it is a threat not only in this region but around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: What I’d also like to point out the Iranians are putting the most lethal IEDs into Iraq which are killing young Americans, there are special groups in Iran coming into Iraq and are being trained in Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There is the Republican Guard in Iran, which Senator Kyl had an amendment in order to declare them a sponsor of terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama said that would be provocative.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So this is a serious threat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This is a serious threat to security in the world, and I believe we can act and we can act with our friends and allies and reduce that threat as quickly as possible, but have no doubt about the ultimate result of them acquiring nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just correct something very quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe the Republican Guard of Iran is a terrorist organization.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve consistently said so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What Senator McCain refers to is a measure in the Senate that would try to broaden the mandate inside of Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: To deal with Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And ironically, the single thing that has strengthened Iran over the last several years has been the war in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Iraq was Iran’s mortal enemy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That was cleared away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what we’ve seen over the last several years is Iran’s influence grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They have funded Hezbollah, they have funded Hamas, they have gone from zero centrifuges to 4,000 centrifuges to develop a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So obviously, our policy over the last eight years has not worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain is absolutely right, we cannot tolerate a nuclear Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It would be a game changer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not only would it threaten Israel, a country that is our stalwart ally, but it would also create an environment in which you could set off an arms race in this Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now here’s what we need to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We do need tougher sanctions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do not agree with Senator McCain that we’re going to be able to execute the kind of sanctions we need without some cooperation with countries like Russia and China that are, I think Senator McCain would agree, not democracies, but have extensive trade with Iran but potentially have an interest in making sure Iran doesn’t have a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we are also going to have to, I believe, engage in tough direct diplomacy with Iran and this is a major difference I have with Senator McCain, this notion that by not talking to people we are punishing them has not worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It has not worked in Iran, it has not worked in North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In each instance, our efforts at isolation have actually accelerated their efforts to get nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That will change when I’m president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama twice said in debates he would sit down with Ahmadinejad, Chavez and Raul Castro without precondition.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Without precondition.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Here is Ahmadinenene , Ahmadinejad, who is, Ahmadinejad, who is now in New York, talking about the extermination of the State of Israel, of wiping Israel off the map, and we’re going to sit down, without precondition, across the table, to legitimize and give a propaganda platform to a person that is espousing the extermination of the state of Israel, and therefore then giving them more credence in the world arena and therefore saying, they’ve probably been doing the right thing, because you will sit down across the table from them and that will legitimize their illegal behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The point is that throughout history, whether it be Ronald Reagan, who wouldn’t sit down with Brezhnev, Andropov or Chernenko until Gorbachev was ready with glasnost and perestroika.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Or whether it be Nixon’s trip to China, which was preceded by Henry Kissinger, many times before he went.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, I’ll sit down with anybody, but there’s got to be pre-conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Those pre-conditions would apply that we wouldn’t legitimize with a face to face meeting, a person like Ahmadinejad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator Obama said, without preconditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So let’s talk about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, Ahmadinejad is not the most powerful person in Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So he may not be the right person to talk to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I reserve the right, as president of the United States to meet with anybody at a time and place of my choosing if I think it’s going to keep America safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’m glad that Senator McCain brought up the history, the bipartisan history of us engaging in direct diplomacy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain mentioned Henry Kissinger, who’s one of his advisers, who, along with five recent secretaries of state, just said that we should meet with Iran — guess what — without precondition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is one of your own advisers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, understand what this means “without preconditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” It doesn’t mean that you invite them over for tea one day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What it means is that we don’t do what we’ve been doing, which is to say, “Until you agree to do exactly what we say, we won’t have direct contacts with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” There’s a difference between preconditions and preparation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Of course we’ve got to do preparations, starting with low-level diplomatic talks, and it may not work, because Iran is a rogue regime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I will point out that I was called naive when I suggested that we need to look at exploring contacts with Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you know what?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: President Bush recently sent a senior ambassador, Bill Burns, to participate in talks with the Europeans around the issue of nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Again, it may not work, but if it doesn’t work, then we have strengthened our ability to form alliances to impose the tough sanctions that Senator McCain just mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when we haven’t done it, as in North Korea — let me just take one more example — in North Korea, we cut off talks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’re a member of the axis of evil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t deal with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you know what happened?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They went — they quadrupled their nuclear capacity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They tested a nuke.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They tested missiles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They pulled out of the nonproliferation agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they sent nuclear secrets, potentially, to countries like Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When we re-engaged — because, again, the Bush administration reversed course on this — then we have at least made some progress, although right now, because of the problems in North Korea, we are seeing it on shaky ground.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And — and I just — so I just have to make this general point that the Bush administration, some of Senator McCain’s own advisers all think this is important, and Senator McCain appears resistant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He even said the other day that he would not meet potentially with the prime minister of Spain, because he — you know, he wasn’t sure whether they were aligned with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, Spain?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Spain is a NATO ally.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we can’t meet with our friends, I don’t know how we’re going to lead the world in terms of dealing with critical issues like terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to set the White House visitors schedule before I’m president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t even have a seal yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Kissinger did not say that he would approve of face-to- face meetings between the president of the United States and the president — and Ahmadinejad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He did not say that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Of course not.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He said that there could be secretary-level and lower level meetings.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve always encouraged them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The Iranians have met with Ambassador Crocker in Baghdad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: What Senator Obama doesn’t seem to understand that if without precondition you sit down across the table from someone who has called Israel a “stinking corpse,” and wants to destroy that country and wipe it off the map, you legitimize those comments.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This is dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It isn’t just naive; it’s dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And so we just have a fundamental difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As far as North Korea is concerned, our secretary of state, Madeleine Albright, went to North Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: By the way, North Korea, most repressive and brutal regime probably on Earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The average South Korean is three inches taller than the average North Korean, a huge gulag.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know what the status of the dear leader’s health is today, but we know this, that the North Koreans have broken every agreement that they’ve entered into.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we ought to go back to a little bit of Ronald Reagan’s “trust, but verify,” and certainly not sit down across the table from — without precondition, as Senator Obama said he did twice, I mean, it’s just dangerous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, I mean, Senator McCain keeps on using this example that suddenly the president would just meet with somebody without doing any preparation, without having low-level talks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nobody’s been talking about that, and Senator McCain knows it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is a mischaracterization of my position.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When we talk about preconditions — and Henry Kissinger did say we should have contacts without preconditions — the idea is that we do not expect to solve every problem before we initiate talks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, the Bush administration has come to recognize that it hasn’t worked, this notion that we are simply silent when it comes to our enemies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the notion that we would sit with Ahmadinejad and not say anything while he’s spewing his nonsense and his vile comments is ridiculous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nobody is even talking about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So let me get this right.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We sit down with Ahmadinejad, and he says, “We’re going to wipe Israel off the face of the Earth,” and we say, “No, you’re not”?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Oh, please.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, let me tell…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: By the way, my friend, Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Kissinger, who’s been my friend for 35 years, would be interested to hear this conversation and Senator Obama’s depiction of his — of his positions on the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve known him for 35 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We will take a look.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I guarantee you he would not — he would not say that presidential top level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nobody’s talking about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course he encourages and other people encourage contacts, and negotiations, and all other things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We do that all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Senator Obama is parsing words when he says precondition means preparation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I am not parsing words.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He’s parsing words, my friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m using the same words that your advisers use.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Please, go ahead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think that, given what’s happened over the last several weeks and months, our entire Russian approach has to be evaluated, because a resurgent and very aggressive Russia is a threat to the peace and stability of the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Their actions in Georgia were unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They were unwarranted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And at this point, it is absolutely critical for the next president to make clear that we have to follow through on our six-party — or the six-point cease-fire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They have to remove themselves from South Ossetia and Abkhazia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is absolutely important that we have a unified alliance and that we explain to the Russians that you cannot be a 21st-century superpower, or power, and act like a 20th-century dictatorship.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we also have to affirm all the fledgling democracies in that region, you know, the Estonians, the Lithuanians, the Latvians, the Poles, the Czechs, that we are, in fact, going to be supportive and in solidarity with them in their efforts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are members of NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And to countries like Georgia and the Ukraine, I think we have to insist that they are free to join NATO if they meet the requirements, and they should have a membership action plan immediately to start bringing them in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, we also can’t return to a Cold War posture with respect to Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s important that we recognize there are going to be some areas of common interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: One is nuclear proliferation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They have not only 15,000 nuclear warheads, but they’ve got enough to make another 40,000, and some of those loose nukes could fall into the hands of Al Qaida.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is an area where I’ve led on in the Senate, working with a Republican ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Dick Lugar, to deal with the proliferation of loose nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s an area where we’re going to have to work with Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we have to have a president who is clear that you don’t deal with Russia based on staring into his eyes and seeing his soul.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You deal with Russia based on, what are your — what are the national security interests of the United States of America?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we have to recognize that the way they’ve been behaving lately demands a sharp response from the international community and our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, I was interested in Senator Obama’s reaction to the Russian aggression against Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: His first statement was, “Both sides ought to show restraint.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” Again, a little bit of naivete there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He doesn’t understand that Russia committed serious aggression against Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Russia has now become a nation fueled by petro-dollars that is basically a KGB apparatchik-run government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I looked into Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Putin’s eyes, and I saw three letters, a “K,” a “G,” and a “B.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” And their aggression in Georgia is not acceptable behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe we’re going to go back to the Cold War.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I am sure that that will not happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I do believe that we need to bolster our friends and allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that wasn’t just about a problem between Georgia and Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It had everything to do with energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There’s a pipeline that runs from the Caspian through Georgia through Turkey.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, of course, we know that the Russians control other sources of energy into Europe, which they have used from time to time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s not accidental that the presidents of Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, Poland, and Ukraine flew to Georgia, flew to Tbilisi, where I have spent significant amount of time with a great young president, Misha Saakashvili.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they showed solidarity with them, but, also, they are very concerned about the Russian threats to regain their status of the old Russian to regain their status of the old Russian empire.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think the Russians ought to understand that we will support — we, the United States — will support the inclusion of Georgia and Ukraine in the natural process, inclusion into NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We also ought to make it very clear that the Russians are in violation of their cease-fire agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They have stationed additional troops in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: By the way, I went there once, and we went inside and drove in, and there was a huge poster.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And this is — this is Georgian territory.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And there was a huge poster of Vladimir Putin, and it said, “Vladimir Putin, our president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” It was very clear, the Russian intentions towards Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They were just waiting to seize the opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So, this is a very difficult situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We want to work with the Russians.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we also have every right to expect the Russians to behave in a fashion and keeping with a — with a — with a country who respects international boundaries and the norms of international behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And watch Ukraine.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This whole thing has got a lot to do with Ukraine, Crimea, the base of the Russian fleet in Sevastopol.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the breakdown of the political process in Ukraine between Tymoshenko and Yushchenko is a very serious problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So watch Ukraine, and let’s make sure that we — that the Ukrainians understand that we are their friend and ally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, actually, I think Senator McCain and I agree for the most part on these issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Obviously, I disagree with this notion that somehow we did not forcefully object to Russians going into Georgia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I immediately said that this was illegal and objectionable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, absolutely, I wanted a cessation of the violence, because it put an enormous strain on Georgia, and that’s why I was the first to say that we have to rebuild the Georgian economy and called for a billion dollars that has now gone in to help them rebuild.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because part of Russia’s intentions here was to weaken the economy to the point where President Saakashvili was so weakened that he might be replaced by somebody that Putin favored more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Two points I think are important to think about when it comes to Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one is we have to have foresight and anticipate some of these problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So back in April, I warned the administration that you had Russian peacekeepers in Georgian territory.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That made no sense whatsoever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what we needed to do was replace them with international peacekeepers and a special envoy to resolve the crisis before it boiled over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But had it been done, it’s possible we could have avoided the issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The second point I want to make is — is the issue of energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Russia is in part resurgent and Putin is feeling powerful because of petro-dollars, as Senator McCain mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That means that we, as one of the biggest consumers of oil — 25 percent of the world’s oil — have to have an energy strategy not just to deal with Russia, but to deal with many of the rogue states we’ve talked about, Iran, Venezuela.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means, yes, increasing domestic production and off-shore drilling, but we only have 3 percent of the world’s oil supplies and we use 25 percent of the world’s oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we can’t simply drill our way out of the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we’re going to have to do is to approach it through alternative energy, like solar, and wind, and biodiesel, and, yes, nuclear energy, clean-coal technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, I’ve got a plan for us to make a significant investment over the next 10 years to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I have to say, Senator McCain and I, I think agree on the importance of energy, but Senator McCain mentioned earlier the importance of looking at a record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Over 26 years, Senator McCain voted 23 times against alternative energy, like solar, and wind, and biodiesel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so we — we — we’ve got to walk the walk and not just talk the talk when it comes to energy independence, because this is probably going to be just as vital for our economy and the pain that people are feeling at the pump — and, you know, winter’s coming and home heating oil — as it is our national security and the issue of climate change that’s so important.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: No one from Arizona is against solar.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And Senator Obama says he’s for nuclear, but he’s against reprocessing and he’s against storing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s just not true, John.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: John, I’m sorry, but that’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … it’s hard to get there from here.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And off-shore drilling is also something that is very important and it is a bridge.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we know that, if we drill off-shore and exploit a lot of these reserves, it will help, at temporarily, relieve our energy requirements.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it will have, I think, an important effect on the price of a barrel of oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I just have to respond very quickly, just to correct — just to correct the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I want to say that, with the Nunn-Lugar thing…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: John?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … I supported Nunn-Lugar back in the early 1990s when a lot of my colleagues didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That was the key legislation at the time and put us on the road to eliminating this issue of nuclear waste and the nuclear fuel that has to be taken care of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I — I just have to correct the record here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I have never said that I object to nuclear waste.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve said is that we have to store it safely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, Senator McCain, he says — he talks about Arizona.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got to make this point, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He objects…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have voted for alternate fuel all of my time…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He — he — he objects…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He objected…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: No one can be opposed to alternate energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: All right, fair enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s move on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got one more energy — you’ve got one more question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s much less than it was the day after 9/11.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think it — that we have a safer nation, but we are a long way from safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I want to tell you that one of the things I’m most proud of, among others, because I have worked across the aisle.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a long record on that, on a long series of reforms.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But after 9/11, Senator Joe Lieberman and I decided that we needed a commission, and that was a commission to investigate 9/11, and find out what happened, and fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we were — we were opposed by the administration, another area where I differed with this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we were stymied until the families of 9/11 came, and they descended on Washington, and we got that legislation passed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And there were a series of recommendations, as I recall, more than 40.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’m happy to say that we’ve gotten written into law most of those reforms recommended by that commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud of that work, again, bipartisan, reaching across the aisle, working together, Democrat and Republican alike.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So we have a long way to go in our intelligence services.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to do a better job in human intelligence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to — to make sure that we have people who are trained interrogators so that we don’t ever torture a prisoner ever again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to make sure that our technological and intelligence capabilities are better.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to work more closely with our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know our allies, and I can work much more closely with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I can tell you that I think America is safer today than it was on 9/11.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But that doesn’t mean that we don’t have a long way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’d like to remind you, also, as a result of those recommendations, we’ve probably had the largest reorganization of government since we established the Defense Department.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I think that those men and women in those agencies are doing a great job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we still have a long way to go before we can declare America safe, and that means doing a better job along our borders, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I think that we are safer in some ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Obviously, we’ve poured billions of dollars into airport security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have done some work in terms of securing potential targets, but we still have a long way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to make sure that we’re hardening our chemical sites.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t done enough in terms of transit; we haven’t done enough in terms of ports.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the biggest threat that we face right now is not a nuclear missile coming over the skies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s in a suitcase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is why the issue of nuclear proliferation is so important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is the — the biggest threat to the United States is a terrorist getting their hands on nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we — we are spending billions of dollars on missile defense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I actually believe that we need missile defense, because of Iran and North Korea and the potential for them to obtain or to launch nuclear weapons, but I also believe that, when we are only spending a few hundred million dollars on nuclear proliferation, then we’re making a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The other thing that we have to focus on, though, is Al Qaida.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are now operating in 60 countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t simply be focused on Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have to go to the root cause, and that is in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to be critical.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are going to need more cooperation with our allies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one last point I want to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is important for us to understand that the way we are perceived in the world is going to make a difference, in terms of our capacity to get cooperation and root out terrorism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things that I intend to do as president is to restore America’s standing in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are less respected now than we were eight years ago or even four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is the greatest country on Earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But because of some of the mistakes that have been made — and I give Senator McCain great credit on the torture issue, for having identified that as something that undermines our long-term security — because of those things, we, I think, are going to have a lot of work to do in the next administration to restore that sense that America is that shining beacon on a hill.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But in the case of missile defense, Senator Obama said it had to be, quote, “proven.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” That wasn’t proven when Ronald Reagan said we would do SDI, which is missile defense.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it was major — a major factor in bringing about the end of the Cold War.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We seem to come full circle again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama still doesn’t quite understand — or doesn’t get it — that if we fail in Iraq, it encourages Al Qaida.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They would establish a base in Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The consequences of defeat, which would result from his plan of withdrawal and according to date certain, regardless of conditions, according to our military leaders, according to every expert, would lead to defeat — possible defeat, loss of all the fragile sacrifice that we’ve made of American blood and treasure, which grieves us all.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: All of that would be lost if we followed Senator Obama’s plan to have specific dates with withdrawal, regardless of conditions on the ground.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And General Petraeus says we have had great success, but it’s very fragile.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we can’t do what Senator Obama wants to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That is the central issue of our time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I think Americans will judge very seriously as to whether that’s the right path or the wrong path and who should be the next president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Oh, there’s no doubt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, over the last eight years, this administration, along with Senator McCain, have been solely focused on Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That has been their priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That has been where all our resources have gone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the meantime, bin Laden is still out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He is not captured.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He is not killed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Al Qaida is resurgent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the meantime, we’ve got challenges, for example, with China, where we are borrowing billions of dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They now hold a trillion dollars’ worth of our debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they are active in countries like — in regions like Latin America, and Asia, and Africa.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are — the conspicuousness of their presence is only matched by our absence, because we’ve been focused on Iraq.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have weakened our capacity to project power around the world because we have viewed everything through this single lens, not to mention, look at our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are now spending $10 billion or more every month.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means we can’t provide health care to people who need it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t invest in science and technology, which will determine whether or not we are going to be competitive in the long term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There has never been a country on Earth that saw its economy decline and yet maintained its military superiority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So this is a national security issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t adequately funded veterans’ care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I sit on the Veterans Affairs Committee, and we’ve got — I meet veterans all across the country who are trying to figure out, “How can I get disability payments?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got post-traumatic stress disorder, and yet I can’t get treatment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” So we have put all chips in, right there, and nobody is talking about losing this war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we are talking about is recognizing that the next president has to have a broader strategic vision about all the challenges that we face.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s been missing over the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That sense is something that I want to restore.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been involved, as I mentioned to you before, in virtually every major national security challenge we’ve faced in the last 20-some years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There are some advantages to experience, and knowledge, and judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I — and I honestly don’t believe that Senator Obama has the knowledge or experience and has made the wrong judgments in a number of areas, including his initial reaction to Russian invasion — aggression in Georgia, to his — you know, we’ve seen this stubbornness before in this administration to cling to a belief that somehow the surge has not succeeded and failing to acknowledge that he was wrong about the surge is — shows to me that we — that — that we need more flexibility in a president of the United States than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As far as our other issues that he brought up are concerned, I know the veterans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know them well.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I know that they know that I’ll take care of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been proud of their support and their recognition of my service to the veterans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I love them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll take care of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they know that I’ll take care of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s going to be my job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But, also, I have the ability, and the knowledge, and the background to make the right judgments, to keep this country safe and secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Reform, prosperity, and peace, these are major challenges to the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think I need any on-the-job training.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m ready to go at it right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just make a closing point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, my father came from Kenya.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s where I get my name.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in the ’60s, he wrote letter after letter to come to college here in the United States because the notion was that there was no other country on Earth where you could make it if you tried.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The ideals and the values of the United States inspired the entire world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think any of us can say that our standing in the world now, the way children around the world look at the United States, is the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And part of what we need to do, what the next president has to do — and this is part of our judgment, this is part of how we’re going to keep America safe — is to — to send a message to the world that we are going to invest in issues like education, we are going to invest in issues that — that relate to how ordinary people are able to live out their dreams.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that is something that I’m going to be committed to as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Jim, when I came home from prison, I saw our veterans being very badly treated, and it made me sad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I embarked on an effort to resolve the POW-MIA issue, which we did in a bipartisan fashion, and then I worked on normalization of relations between our two countries so that our veterans could come all the way home.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I guarantee you, as president of the United States, I know how to heal the wounds of war, I know how to deal with our adversaries, and I know how to deal with our friends.
